plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter, producing fragrant blossoms. It is widely cultivated in Japan, China, and Korea and is prized in gardens and bonsai. The flowers are followed by sour fruits used for pickling and liqueur.
plants.location: East Asia (China, Japan, Korea); cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance and hope in East Asian culture because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like petals that bloom on leafless branches in winter. The flowers have a strong, sweet spicy fragrance and tolerate frost by curling up in the cold and unfurling again when it warms.
plants.location: Central and eastern China; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel petals curl into tight spirals during freezing weather to protect themselves, then relax again once temperatures rise.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad-canopied tropical tree that produces spectacular clusters of large flowers. In parts of the Southern Hemisphere, such as Australia and southern Africa, it blooms in the summer heat, making a striking display against its fern-like foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); other tropical regions at different times
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, southern Africa, South America, and tropical regions
plants.funFact: The royal poinciana is native to Madagascar but is now endangered in the wild, even though it is one of the most commonly planted ornamental trees in the tropics.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial whose nodding white flowers push up through snow and frozen ground. In mild parts of Britain, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest, snowdrops are often in full bloom by late January, carpeting woodlands and gardens.
plants.location: Europe and southwest Asia; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.
